result.summary: Do not ship: password changes no longer revoke compromised sessions.

findings.title: Stolen session cookies retain access after password changes
findings.body: A stolen, unexpired triggarr_session cookie remains usable after POST /settings/password succeeds because this update preserves session_secret. AuthMiddleware accepts that cookie at triggarr/web/middleware.py:144–148 without checking the password hash; validate_session only checks its signature and 30-day age. An attacker therefore retains authenticated access for the cookie's remaining lifetime despite the owner's password change. The removed secret rotation previously blocked this exact path; rotation in the separate reset endpoint does not protect password changes. Existing test_password_change_invalidates_old_sessions explicitly requires rejection of the old cookie.
findings.recommendation: Restore session-secret rotation alongside the password-hash update and reissue the acting user's cookie under the new secret. Verify that a second client's pre-change cookie is rejected.

next_steps: Restore revocation and run the password-change session lifecycle tests.
